samasa.type: karmadhāraya (śrī as qualifying/honorific first member); alternatively ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa
samasa.vigraha: श्रीः माता श्रीमाता (श्रीः च असौ माता च); अथवा श्रियः माता श्रीमाता
samasa.vigraha_iast: śrīḥ mātā śrīmātā (śrīḥ ca asau mātā ca); athavā śriyaḥ mātā śrīmātā
samasa.explanation: Two analyses are current, and both make mātā 'mother' the head. As a karmadhāraya, śrī stands in apposition to mātā: 'the Mother who is Śrī', i.e. auspicious, glorious, the source of all prosperity. As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, śrī is the goddess Śrī (Lakṣmī): 'the mother of Śrī'. Śrī and mātā are simply juxtaposed; there is no sound change.

components.meaning: auspiciousness, glory, splendor; also the goddess Śrī (Lakṣmī)

components.note: nominative singular of the stem mātṛ

names.meaning: She who is the auspicious Mother
names.significance: Traditionally the first three names are read together as the three cosmic functions: as Mother She brings forth the worlds (sṛṣṭi), as Empress She sustains them (sthiti), and as Sovereign of the lion-throne She withdraws them (saṃhāra). She is Mother even of Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī.
names.uncertain: Two compound analyses are current: karmadhāraya ('the auspicious Mother') and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('Mother of Śrī/Lakṣmī'). The meaning follows the first; the second is given in the samāsa note.

samasa.explanation: Inner layer: mahatī rājñī 'the great queen'. In a karmadhāraya the feminine adjective mahatī takes its masculine stem (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42), and mahat then becomes mahā- before a co-referential member (6.3.46 ān mahataḥ samānādhikaraṇa-jātīyayoḥ): mahā-rājñī. Rājñī is the feminine of rājan 'king' and is the head. Outer layer: śrī qualifies mahārājñī as in name 1. These are morphological replacements, not sound-sandhi; the members meet without phonetic change.

samasa.explanation: Inner layer: the adjective śrīmat 'glorious' qualifies siṃhāsana 'lion-seat, throne' (karmadhāraya). Outer layer: īśvarī 'sovereign, ruling lady' is the head and the throne stands to it in the genitive relation: 'the sovereign of the glorious throne'. Grammatically śrīmat could also qualify the sovereign herself (śrīmatī reduced to śrīmat by puṃvadbhāva), but the usual reading attaches it to the throne.

samasa.vigraha_iast: cit eva agniḥ cidagniḥ; cidagneḥ kuṇḍam cidagnikuṇḍam; cidagnikuṇḍāt sambhūtā cidagnikuṇḍasambhūtā
samasa.explanation: Built in three layers. (1) cit-agni 'the fire that is consciousness': a karmadhāraya of identification (rūpaka) — consciousness itself is the fire. (2) cidagni-kuṇḍa 'the altar-pit of that fire': ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, kuṇḍa is the head. (3) The participle sambhūtā 'arisen' is the head of the whole and the fire-pit stands to it in the ablative: 'arisen from'. A locative reading (cidagnikuṇḍe sambhūtā, saptamī-tatpuruṣa, 'born in the fire-pit') is also current; the sense hardly changes.

names.meaning: She who arose from the fire-altar of pure consciousness
names.significance: In the Lalitopākhyāna of the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa the Goddess appears from the sacrificial fire kindled by the gods for the war against Bhaṇḍa. Inwardly, the fire is consciousness itself, in which ignorance and duality are offered up.

meaning_check.note: 'fire-pit of Pure Consciousness' blurred the inner rūpaka: the fire is consciousness and the kuṇḍa is that fire's altar-pit; capitalization tidied.

names.uncertain: Ablative ('arisen from') and locative ('born in') analyses of the last member are both current.

names.significance: In the Purāṇa the gods' task is the destruction of the demon Bhaṇḍa, for which She arose (name 4). Traditionally it is also read as Her readiness to protect all who live by dharma.

samasa.vigraha_iast: udyantaḥ bhānavaḥ udyadbhānavaḥ; udyadbhānūnām sahasram udyadbhānusahasram; udyadbhānusahasrasya ābhā iva ābhā yasyāḥ sā udyadbhānusahasrābhā
samasa.explanation: (1) udyad-bhānu 'rising sun(s)': the present participle udyat qualifies bhānu (karmadhāraya). (2) udyadbhānu-sahasra 'a thousand rising suns' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, sahasra is the head). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She whose radiance (ābhā) is like that of a thousand rising suns'. The name could also be taken as a tatpuruṣa in apposition ('She who is the radiance of …'); the image is the same.

names.meaning: She who has the radiance of a thousand rising suns
names.significance: The crimson of the rising sun is Her own color throughout the hymn; 'a thousand' is traditionally taken to mean beyond counting, a brilliance that is nonetheless gentle like dawn.

samasa.explanation: Inner layer: catur-bāhu 'four arms', a numeral + noun karmadhāraya, i.e. a dvigu, allowed here because another member follows (Pāṇini 2.1.51–52). Outer layer: the participle samanvitā 'endowed with' is the head and the four arms stand to it in the instrumental. The r of catur is original, so it stays r before the voiced b; no visarga arises.

names.meaning: She who is four-armed
names.significance: The four arms carry the four emblems named next: the noose, the goad, the sugarcane bow and the flower arrows (names 8–11).

samasa.vigraha_iast: rāgaḥ svarūpam yasya saḥ rāgasvarūpaḥ; rāgasvarūpaḥ pāśaḥ rāgasvarūpapāśaḥ; rāgasvarūpapāśena āḍhyā rāgasvarūpapāśāḍhyā
samasa.explanation: (1) rāga-svarūpa 'whose very nature is desire' — a bahuvrīhi that qualifies the noose. (2) rāgasvarūpa-pāśa 'the noose whose nature is desire' (karmadhāraya, pāśa is the head). (3) āḍhyā 'rich in, furnished with' is the head of the whole and takes the noose in the instrumental: 'furnished with that noose'.

names.meaning: She who holds the noose whose very nature is desire (rāga)
names.significance: In Śrīvidyā the noose is commonly read as icchā-śakti, the power of will: the binding pull of attachment is itself held in Her hand, so She can bind devotees to Herself and loosen worldly ties.

meaning_check.note: The noose is 'of the nature of rāga' (desire/attachment); āḍhyā means 'furnished with', so 'holding' is kept, but 'rope of love' narrowed rāga.

samasa.explanation: Parallel to name 8. (1) krodha-ākāra 'whose form is anger' — a bahuvrīhi qualifying the goad. (2) krodhākāra-aṅkuśa 'the goad that has the form of anger' (karmadhāraya). (3) ujjvalā 'blazing, resplendent' is the head and takes the goad in the instrumental: 'resplendent with that goad'. Every junction fuses its vowels, so the name cannot be hyphenated.

names.meaning: She who is resplendent with the goad that has the form of anger
names.significance: The goad restrains and directs, as the noose binds. In Śrīvidyā it is commonly read as jñāna-śakti, the power of knowledge; anger itself, held by Her, becomes a force that curbs what is wrong.

samasa.vigraha_iast: campakaḥ ca aśokaḥ ca punnāgaḥ ca saugandhikam ca campakāśokapunnāgasaugandhikāni; campakāśokapunnāgasaugandhikaiḥ lasantaḥ kacāḥ yasyāḥ sā campakāśokapunnāgasaugandhikalasatkacā
samasa.explanation: (1) The four flower names form an itaretara-dvandva, 'campaka, aśoka, punnāga and saugandhika (blossoms)'. (2) They stand in the instrumental to the participle lasat 'shining, playing' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) lasat qualifies kaca 'hair, tresses' (karmadhāraya). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She whose tresses shine with …'; kaca takes the feminine -ā.

samasa.vigraha: कुरुविन्दाः मणयः कुरुविन्दमणयः; कुरुविन्दमणीनाम् श्रेणी कुरुविन्दमणिश्रेणी; कुरुविन्दमणिश्रेण्या कनत् कोटीरम् कुरुविन्दमणिश्रेणीकनत्कोटीरम्; तेन मण्डिता कुरुविन्दमणिश्रेणीकनत्कोटीरमण्डिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: kuruvindāḥ maṇayaḥ kuruvindamaṇayaḥ; kuruvindamaṇīnām śreṇī kuruvindamaṇiśreṇī; kuruvindamaṇiśreṇyā kanat koṭīram kuruvindamaṇiśreṇīkanatkoṭīram; tena maṇḍitā kuruvindamaṇiśreṇīkanatkoṭīramaṇḍitā
samasa.explanation: (1) kuruvinda-maṇi 'kuruvinda gems', i.e. rubies (karmadhāraya). (2) …maṇi-śreṇī 'a row of them' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) …śreṇī-kanat 'sparkling with that row' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa with the participle kanat), which qualifies koṭīra 'crown' (karmadhāraya). (4) The past participle maṇḍitā 'adorned' is the head of the whole and takes the crown in the instrumental. The members meet without sound change.

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner upamāna-karmadhāraya, a karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: अष्टम्याः चन्द्रः अष्टमीचन्द्रः; अष्टमीचन्द्रः इव विभ्राजत् अष्टमीचन्द्रविभ्राजत्; अलिकस्य स्थलम् अलिकस्थलम्; अष्टमीचन्द्रविभ्राजत् अलिकस्थलम् अष्टमीचन्द्रविभ्राजदलिकस्थलम्; तेन शोभिता अष्टमीचन्द्रविभ्राजदलिकस्थलशोभिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: aṣṭamyāḥ candraḥ aṣṭamīcandraḥ; aṣṭamīcandraḥ iva vibhrājat aṣṭamīcandravibhrājat; alikasya sthalam alikasthalam; aṣṭamīcandravibhrājat alikasthalam aṣṭamīcandravibhrājadalikasthalam; tena śobhitā aṣṭamīcandravibhrājadalikasthalaśobhitā
samasa.explanation: (1) aṣṭamī-candra 'the moon of the eighth lunar day', the half-moon (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) aṣṭamīcandra-vibhrājat 'shining like that moon': the standard of comparison compounded with the word for the shared quality (upamāna-karmadhāraya, Pāṇini 2.1.55 upamānāni sāmānyavacanaiḥ, as in ghana-śyāma 'dark as a cloud'). (3) alika-sthala 'the expanse of the forehead' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), qualified by (2) (karmadhāraya). (4) The participle śobhitā 'beautified' is the head and takes the forehead in the instrumental.

names.meaning: She whose forehead shines like the half-moon of the eighth lunar day

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya, a bahuvrīhi of resemblance, a rūpaka-karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-/tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: मुखम् एव चन्द्रः मुखचन्द्रः; मुखचन्द्रस्य कलङ्कः मुखचन्द्रकलङ्कः; मुखचन्द्रकलङ्कस्य आभा इव आभा यस्य सः मुखचन्द्रकलङ्काभः; मृगस्य नाभिः मृगनाभिः; मृगनाभिना कृतः विशेषकः मृगनाभिविशेषकः; मुखचन्द्रकलङ्काभः मृगनाभिविशेषकः यस्याः सा मुखचन्द्रकलङ्काभमृगनाभिविशेषका
samasa.vigraha_iast: mukham eva candraḥ mukhacandraḥ; mukhacandrasya kalaṅkaḥ mukhacandrakalaṅkaḥ; mukhacandrakalaṅkasya ābhā iva ābhā yasya saḥ mukhacandrakalaṅkābhaḥ; mṛgasya nābhiḥ mṛganābhiḥ; mṛganābhinā kṛtaḥ viśeṣakaḥ mṛganābhiviśeṣakaḥ; mukhacandrakalaṅkābhaḥ mṛganābhiviśeṣakaḥ yasyāḥ sā mukhacandrakalaṅkābhamṛganābhiviśeṣakā
samasa.explanation: (1) mukha-candra 'the moon that is (Her) face' (rūpaka-karmadhāraya: the face is identified with the moon). (2) …candra-kalaṅka 'the dark mark on that moon' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) …kalaṅka-ābha 'looking like that mark' (bahuvrīhi of resemblance), qualifying (4) mṛganābhi-viśeṣaka 'a forehead-mark (tilaka) of musk' (mṛga-nābhi 'deer's navel' = musk, then a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa of material). (3) and (4) form a karmadhāraya. (5) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose musk tilaka looks like the mark on the moon of Her face'.

names.meaning: She whose musk tilaka looks like the dark mark on the moon of Her face
names.significance: The face is the full moon and the dark musk mark on the forehead is its 'spot': the blemish of the real moon becomes an ornament on Hers.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi of comparison (over a rūpaka-karmadhāraya, a karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: माङ्गल्यम् गृहम् माङ्गल्यगृहम्; स्मरस्य माङ्गल्यगृहम् स्मरमाङ्गल्यगृहम्; वदनम् एव स्मरमाङ्गल्यगृहम् वदनस्मरमाङ्गल्यगृहम्; वदनस्मरमाङ्गल्यगृहस्य तोरणम् वदनस्मरमाङ्गल्यगृहतोरणम्; तत् इव चिल्लिके यस्याः सा वदनस्मरमाङ्गल्यगृहतोरणचिल्लिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: māṅgalyam gṛham māṅgalyagṛham; smarasya māṅgalyagṛham smaramāṅgalyagṛham; vadanam eva smaramāṅgalyagṛham vadanasmaramāṅgalyagṛham; vadanasmaramāṅgalyagṛhasya toraṇam vadanasmaramāṅgalyagṛhatoraṇam; tat iva cillike yasyāḥ sā vadanasmaramāṅgalyagṛhatoraṇacillikā
samasa.explanation: (1) māṅgalya-gṛha 'festive, auspicious house' (karmadhāraya). (2) smara-… 'Kāma's festive house' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) vadana-… 'the face, which is Kāma's festive house' (rūpaka-karmadhāraya). (4) …gṛha-toraṇa 'the arched gateway of that house' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (5) A bahuvrīhi of comparison: 'She whose eyebrows are (like) that gateway'. The feminine cillikā, as a subordinate final member, is shortened (Pāṇini 1.2.48 gostriyor upasarjanasya) and then takes -ā again to agree with Her.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner bahuvrīhi of resemblance, a karmadhāraya, a saptamī-tatpuruṣa and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: वक्त्रस्य लक्ष्मीः वक्त्रलक्ष्मीः; वक्त्रलक्ष्म्याः परीवाहः वक्त्रलक्ष्मीपरीवाहः; वक्त्रलक्ष्मीपरीवाहे चलन्तौ मीनौ; तयोः आभा इव आभा ययोः ते वक्त्रलक्ष्मीपरीवाहचलन्मीनाभे लोचने; ते लोचने यस्याः सा वक्त्रलक्ष्मीपरीवाहचलन्मीनाभलोचना
samasa.vigraha_iast: vaktrasya lakṣmīḥ vaktralakṣmīḥ; vaktralakṣmyāḥ parīvāhaḥ vaktralakṣmīparīvāhaḥ; vaktralakṣmīparīvāhe calantau mīnau; tayoḥ ābhā iva ābhā yayoḥ te vaktralakṣmīparīvāhacalanmīnābhe locane; te locane yasyāḥ sā vaktralakṣmīparīvāhacalanmīnābhalocanā
samasa.explanation: (1) vaktra-lakṣmī 'the beauty of the face' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; lakṣmī here means beauty, not the goddess). (2) …lakṣmī-parīvāha 'the overflowing stream of that beauty' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) …parīvāha-calat 'darting in that stream' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa with the participle), qualifying mīna 'fish' (karmadhāraya). (4) …mīna-ābha 'looking like those fish' (bahuvrīhi of resemblance), qualifying locana 'eye'. (5) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose eyes are like fish darting in the stream of Her face's beauty'.

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya, a bahuvrīhi of resemblance and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: चम्पकस्य पुष्पम् चम्पकपुष्पम्; नवम् चम्पकपुष्पम् नवचम्पकपुष्पम्; नवचम्पकपुष्पस्य आभा इव आभा यस्य सः नवचम्पकपुष्पाभः; नासायाः दण्डः नासादण्डः; नवचम्पकपुष्पाभः नासादण्डः नवचम्पकपुष्पाभनासादण्डः; तेन विराजिता नवचम्पकपुष्पाभनासादण्डविराजिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: campakasya puṣpam campakapuṣpam; navam campakapuṣpam navacampakapuṣpam; navacampakapuṣpasya ābhā iva ābhā yasya saḥ navacampakapuṣpābhaḥ; nāsāyāḥ daṇḍaḥ nāsādaṇḍaḥ; navacampakapuṣpābhaḥ nāsādaṇḍaḥ navacampakapuṣpābhanāsādaṇḍaḥ; tena virājitā navacampakapuṣpābhanāsādaṇḍavirājitā
samasa.explanation: (1) nava-campakapuṣpa 'a fresh campaka blossom' (karmadhāraya over the ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa campaka-puṣpa). (2) …puṣpa-ābha 'resembling that blossom' (bahuvrīhi of resemblance), qualifying (3) nāsā-daṇḍa 'the staff of the nose', i.e. its straight ridge (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) The participle virājitā 'shining, made resplendent' is the head and takes the nose in the instrumental.

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya, an upapada-tatpuruṣa and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: ताराणाम् कान्तिः ताराकान्तिः; ताराकान्तिम् तिरस्करोति इति ताराकान्तितिरस्कारि; नासायाः आभरणम् नासाभरणम्; ताराकान्तितिरस्कारि नासाभरणम् ताराकान्तितिरस्कारिनासाभरणम्; तेन भासुरा ताराकान्तितिरस्कारिनासाभरणभासुरा
samasa.vigraha_iast: tārāṇām kāntiḥ tārākāntiḥ; tārākāntim tiraskaroti iti tārākāntitiraskāri; nāsāyāḥ ābharaṇam nāsābharaṇam; tārākāntitiraskāri nāsābharaṇam tārākāntitiraskārināsābharaṇam; tena bhāsurā tārākāntitiraskārināsābharaṇabhāsurā
samasa.explanation: (1) tārā-kānti 'the brilliance of the stars' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) …kānti-tiraskārin 'putting that brilliance to shame': an agent noun in -in from tiras + √kṛ, compounded with its object (upapada-tatpuruṣa); it loses its final n in composition (8.2.7). (3) It qualifies nāsā-ābharaṇa 'nose-ornament' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa) as a karmadhāraya. (4) bhāsurā 'radiant' is the head and takes the ornament in the instrumental.

from √bhās 'to shine'

names.meaning: She who shines with a nose-ornament that excels the luster of a star
names.significance: The jewel of Her nose-ornament outshines the stars; traditionally the ornament is pictured as set with a pearl or gem.

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya, a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: कदम्बस्य मञ्जर्यः कदम्बमञ्जर्यः; कदम्बमञ्जरीभिः कॢप्तः कदम्बमञ्जरीकॢप्तः; कदम्बमञ्जरीकॢप्तः कर्णपूरः कदम्बमञ्जरीकॢप्तकर्णपूरः; तेन मनोहरा कदम्बमञ्जरीकॢप्तकर्णपूरमनोहरा
samasa.vigraha_iast: kadambasya mañjaryaḥ kadambamañjaryaḥ; kadambamañjarībhiḥ kḷptaḥ kadambamañjarīkḷptaḥ; kadambamañjarīkḷptaḥ karṇapūraḥ kadambamañjarīkḷptakarṇapūraḥ; tena manoharā kadambamañjarīkḷptakarṇapūramanoharā
samasa.explanation: (1) kadamba-mañjarī 'clusters of kadamba blossom' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) …mañjarī-kḷpta 'fashioned from those clusters': an instrument compounded with a past participle (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, Pāṇini 2.1.32 kartṛkaraṇe kṛtā bahulam). (3) It qualifies karṇapūra 'ear-ornament' (karmadhāraya). (4) manoharā 'captivating' is the head and takes the ornament in the instrumental: 'captivating with …'.

names.meaning: She who is captivating with ear-ornaments fashioned from clusters of kadamba blossoms
names.significance: The kadamba is Her tree: She dwells in the kadamba forest (kadambavana) of Her island-city, and its blossoms adorn Her ears.

meaning_check.note: Reworded to follow the compound: the ear-ornaments are fashioned (kḷpta) from the kadamba clusters.

names.previous_split_issues: klṛpta was misspelt (the participle of √kḷp is kḷpta, corrected in the text), and karṇapūra 'ear-ornament' was cut into karṇa + pūra with pūra glossed 'ornament/fullness'.
names.variants: Many printed editions spell the participle क्लृप्त (klṛpta); कॢप्त (kḷpta) is the correct form, as in name 648.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya, a gati-samāsa with a cvi form, an itaretara-dvandva and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: ताटङ्कयोः युगलम् ताटङ्कयुगलम्; अताटङ्कयुगलम् ताटङ्कयुगलम् भूते ताटङ्कयुगलीभूते; तपनः च उडुपः च तपनोडुपौ; तपनोडुपयोः मण्डले तपनोडुपमण्डले; ताटङ्कयुगलीभूते तपनोडुपमण्डले यस्याः सा ताटङ्कयुगलीभूततपनोडुपमण्डला
samasa.vigraha_iast: tāṭaṅkayoḥ yugalam tāṭaṅkayugalam; atāṭaṅkayugalam tāṭaṅkayugalam bhūte tāṭaṅkayugalībhūte; tapanaḥ ca uḍupaḥ ca tapanoḍupau; tapanoḍupayoḥ maṇḍale tapanoḍupamaṇḍale; tāṭaṅkayugalībhūte tapanoḍupamaṇḍale yasyāḥ sā tāṭaṅkayugalībhūtatapanoḍupamaṇḍalā
samasa.explanation: (1) tāṭaṅka-yugala 'a pair of earrings' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) With the suffix cvi ('becoming what it was not') its final a becomes ī (Pāṇini 7.4.32 asya cvau), and the cvi form, a gati (1.4.61), compounds with bhūta 'become' (2.2.18 kugatiprādayaḥ): tāṭaṅkayugalī-bhūta 'turned into a pair of earrings'. (3) tapana-uḍupa 'sun and moon' (itaretara-dvandva) + maṇḍala 'disc' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) (2) qualifies (3) (karmadhāraya). (5) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She for whom the discs of sun and moon have become a pair of earrings'.

components.note: yugala 'pair' + cvi: a → ī (Pāṇini 7.4.32)
√bhū 'to be, become', past participle
maṇḍala, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She for whom the discs of the sun and the moon have become a pair of earrings
names.significance: Sun and moon are mere ornaments of Her cosmic form. The earrings are also the sign of auspicious wedded life: Saundaryalaharī 28 says Śiva survived the poison he swallowed by the power of Her tāṭaṅka.

meaning_check.note: 'large' is not in the name; the cvi form means the sun and moon have 'become' the earrings.

names.previous_split_issues: yugalī was glossed simply 'pair'; it is the cvi form (yugala → yugalī) and makes one unit with bhūta, 'turned into a pair'. tapanoḍupa was left fused (tapana + uḍupa).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya, an upapada-tatpuruṣa and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: पद्मरागस्य शिला पद्मरागशिला; पद्मरागशिलामयः आदर्शः पद्मरागशिलादर्शः; पद्मरागशिलादर्शम् परिभवति इति पद्मरागशिलादर्शपरिभाविनी; कपोलयोः भूः कपोलभूः; पद्मरागशिलादर्शपरिभाविनी कपोलभूः यस्याः सा पद्मरागशिलादर्शपरिभाविकपोलभूः
samasa.vigraha_iast: padmarāgasya śilā padmarāgaśilā; padmarāgaśilāmayaḥ ādarśaḥ padmarāgaśilādarśaḥ; padmarāgaśilādarśam paribhavati iti padmarāgaśilādarśaparibhāvinī; kapolayoḥ bhūḥ kapolabhūḥ; padmarāgaśilādarśaparibhāvinī kapolabhūḥ yasyāḥ sā padmarāgaśilādarśaparibhāvikapolabhūḥ
samasa.explanation: (1) padmarāga-śilā 'a slab of ruby' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) …śilā-ādarśa 'a mirror made of such a slab' (karmadhāraya with the middle word -maya dropped). (3) …ādarśa-paribhāvin 'surpassing that mirror' (upapada-tatpuruṣa; agent noun in -in from pari + √bhū). (4) kapola-bhū 'the expanse of the cheeks' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (5) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose cheeks surpass …'. The feminine paribhāvinī takes the masculine stem in the bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.34) and drops its n (8.2.7); bhū is not a feminine-suffix stem, so it is not shortened and keeps its nominative -bhūḥ.

components.note: pari + √bhū 'to overcome' + -in; appears as paribhāvi- in the compound
nominative of bhū; here 'the surface of the cheeks'

names.meaning: She whose cheeks outshine mirrors made of ruby (padmarāga)
names.significance: Her cheeks are so clear and rosy that they put to shame mirrors of polished ruby — the red of Her form once more, now as a reflecting surface.

meaning_check.note: Light tidy: paribhāvin 'putting to shame, outshining'; 'in their beauty' is implied, not stated.

names.previous_split_issues: bhūḥ was glossed 'surface/earth' — 'earth' does not apply; kapola-bhū is the expanse of the cheeks.

sandhi.rule: after a short vowel, ch is preceded by the augment t (Pāṇini 6.1.73 che ca), which becomes c before ch (8.4.40 stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ): -acch-

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya, an itaretara-dvandva, an upapada-tatpuruṣa and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: नवः विद्रुमः नवविद्रुमः; नवविद्रुमः च बिम्बम् च नवविद्रुमबिम्बे; नवविद्रुमबिम्बयोः श्रीः नवविद्रुमबिम्बश्रीः; नवविद्रुमबिम्बश्रियम् न्यक्करोति इति नवविद्रुमबिम्बश्रीन्यक्कारी; रदनानाम् छदः रदनच्छदः; नवविद्रुमबिम्बश्रीन्यक्कारिणौ रदनच्छदौ यस्याः सा नवविद्रुमबिम्बश्रीन्यक्कारिरदनच्छदा
samasa.vigraha_iast: navaḥ vidrumaḥ navavidrumaḥ; navavidrumaḥ ca bimbam ca navavidrumabimbe; navavidrumabimbayoḥ śrīḥ navavidrumabimbaśrīḥ; navavidrumabimbaśriyam nyakkaroti iti navavidrumabimbaśrīnyakkārī; radanānām chadaḥ radanacchadaḥ; navavidrumabimbaśrīnyakkāriṇau radanacchadau yasyāḥ sā navavidrumabimbaśrīnyakkāriradanacchadā
samasa.explanation: (1) nava-vidruma 'fresh coral' (karmadhāraya). (2) …vidruma-bimba 'fresh coral and the bimba fruit' (itaretara-dvandva). (3) …bimba-śrī 'their beauty' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) …śrī-nyakkārin 'humbling that beauty' (upapada-tatpuruṣa; agent noun in -in from nyak + √kṛ, final n dropped). (5) radana-chada 'the covering of the teeth', i.e. the lip (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), qualified by (4). (6) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose lips humble the beauty of fresh coral and the bimba fruit'.

components.meaning: the bimba fruit (ivy gourd), bright red when ripe

components.note: nyak 'down' + √kṛ + -in; appears as nyakkāri- in the compound
chada, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose lips put to shame the beauty of fresh coral and of the bimba fruit
names.significance: Coral and the ripe bimba are the poets' standard images for red lips; Hers surpass both.

meaning_check.note: 'reflective splendor' was a misreading (bimba here is the red fruit, not 'reflection'); 'freshly cut' is not in the name.

names.previous_split_issues: śrī was glossed 'sacred/auspicious'; here it means beauty. radanacchadā was left fused (radana 'tooth' + chadā 'covering').

savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhārayas, a bahuvrīhi of resemblance and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: शुद्धा विद्या शुद्धविद्या; शुद्धविद्यायाः अङ्कुराः शुद्धविद्याङ्कुराः; शुद्धविद्याङ्कुराणाम् आकारः इव आकारः येषाम् ते शुद्धविद्याङ्कुराकाराः; शुद्धविद्याङ्कुराकाराः द्विजाः शुद्धविद्याङ्कुराकारद्विजाः; तेषाम् पङ्क्त्योः द्वयम् शुद्धविद्याङ्कुराकारद्विजपङ्क्तिद्वयम्; तेन उज्ज्वला शुद्धविद्याङ्कुराकारद्विजपङ्क्तिद्वयोज्ज्वला
samasa.vigraha_iast: śuddhā vidyā śuddhavidyā; śuddhavidyāyāḥ aṅkurāḥ śuddhavidyāṅkurāḥ; śuddhavidyāṅkurāṇām ākāraḥ iva ākāraḥ yeṣām te śuddhavidyāṅkurākārāḥ; śuddhavidyāṅkurākārāḥ dvijāḥ śuddhavidyāṅkurākāradvijāḥ; teṣām paṅktyoḥ dvayam śuddhavidyāṅkurākāradvijapaṅktidvayam; tena ujjvalā śuddhavidyāṅkurākāradvijapaṅktidvayojjvalā
samasa.explanation: (1) śuddha-vidyā 'pure knowledge' (karmadhāraya; śuddhā takes its masculine stem, Pāṇini 6.3.42). (2) …vidyā-aṅkura 'the sprouts of pure knowledge' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) …aṅkura-ākāra 'shaped like those sprouts' (bahuvrīhi of resemblance), qualifying dvija 'tooth' (karmadhāraya). (4) …dvija-paṅkti-dvaya 'the two rows of those teeth' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (5) ujjvalā 'resplendent' is the head and takes the two rows in the instrumental.

components.note: ud + √jval 'to blaze', feminine

names.meaning: She who is resplendent with two rows of teeth shaped like the sprouts of pure knowledge (śuddhavidyā)
names.significance: Traditionally śuddhavidyā is taken here as the sixteen-syllabled Śrīvidyā mantra (ṣoḍaśī), the two rows of sixteen teeth answering to it; Her very smile shows the white, budding seeds of liberating knowledge.

meaning_check.note: The name speaks of two rows (paṅkti-dvaya) and of sprouts (aṅkura), not buds.

names.previous_split_issues: śuddha was split from vidyā while vidyā, aṅkura and ākāra were lumped into one row, and dvaya + ujjvalā were lumped as 'dvayojjvalā'.
names.uncertain: The identification of śuddhavidyā with the sixteen-syllabled mantra (and of the 32 teeth with it) is widely reported from the commentarial tradition; its exact source wording was not confirmed here.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the second member is āmoda 'fragrance', not moda 'joy' — the fused ā hides the difference
the final of diś becomes a velar at the end of a member (Pāṇini 8.2.62 kvinpratyayasya kuḥ), voiced to g by jaśtva (8.2.39): dig-

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya, an upapada-tatpuruṣa and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas)
samasa.vigraha: कर्पूरयुक्ता वीटिका कर्पूरवीटिका; कर्पूरवीटिकायाः आमोदः कर्पूरवीटिकामोदः; कर्पूरवीटिकामोदम् समाकर्षन्ति इति कर्पूरवीटिकामोदसमाकर्षीणि; दिशाम् अन्तराणि दिगन्तराणि; कर्पूरवीटिकामोदसमाकर्षीणि दिगन्तराणि यस्याः सा कर्पूरवीटिकामोदसमाकर्षिदिगन्तरा
samasa.vigraha_iast: karpūrayuktā vīṭikā karpūravīṭikā; karpūravīṭikāyāḥ āmodaḥ karpūravīṭikāmodaḥ; karpūravīṭikāmodam samākarṣanti iti karpūravīṭikāmodasamākarṣīṇi; diśām antarāṇi digantarāṇi; karpūravīṭikāmodasamākarṣīṇi digantarāṇi yasyāḥ sā karpūravīṭikāmodasamākarṣidigantarā
samasa.explanation: (1) karpūra-vīṭikā 'a betel roll with camphor' (karmadhāraya with the middle word 'yukta, containing' dropped). (2) …vīṭikā-āmoda 'its fragrance' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) …āmoda-samākarṣin 'drawing in that fragrance' (upapada-tatpuruṣa; agent noun in -in from sam + ā + √kṛṣ, final n dropped). (4) dig-antara 'the reaches of the quarters' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), qualified by (3). (5) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose quarters of space draw in the fragrance of Her camphor-betel', i.e. the fragrance pervades every direction.

components.meaning: betel roll (tāmbūla), folded betel leaf with areca and spices

components.note: sam + ā + √kṛṣ 'to draw' + -in; appears as samākarṣi- in the compound
antara, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose fragrance of camphor-scented betel draws in all the quarters of space
names.significance: Traditionally read as the fragrance of Her betel pervading every direction and drawing beings from all quarters to Her. Betel with camphor is among the offerings (upacāra) of Her worship.

meaning_check.note: 'is enjoying' and 'people' are not in the name; the second member is āmoda 'fragrance'. The wording keeps the compound's relation between the fragrance and the quarters.

names.previous_split_issues: The split cut vīṭikā + 'moda'; the member is āmoda 'fragrance' (its ā merged with vīṭikā's). digantarā was left as one row (diś + antarā).
names.uncertain: The relation of samākarṣin to digantara admits two readings: the quarters draw in (are pervaded by) the fragrance, as analysed here, or the fragrance draws the beings of every quarter to Her, the usual paraphrase, which takes digantara by metonymy for those who dwell there.

verse_notes.note: Names 1–3 each open with śrī/śrīmat and are traditionally read together as creation, maintenance and dissolution; names 4–5 begin the Purāṇic account of Her appearance from the fire for the gods' task.
Names 8–11 (running into śloka 3) name the four emblems held in the four hands of name 7.
Name 12 fills the whole second half; its participle majjat 'sinking' is intransitive (the universe is immersed).
From name 13 the names describe Her form from the hair downward; from here to śloka 10 each half-śloka is a single name.
Name 15: divide vibhrājad-alika ('shining forehead'), not vibhrāja-dalika; the d is the voiced t of the participle vibhrājat.
Both names are layered bahuvrīhis built on an identification: the face as Kāma's festive house (17), the face's beauty as a stream (18).
Name 21 is spelled with vocalic ḷ: कॢप्त (kḷpta), the participle of √kḷp; karṇapūra 'ear-ornament' is one word.
Name 23 ends in the ū-stem bhū, so its nominative ends -bhūḥ, not -ā; the visarga stands at the half-line break.
Name 26: vīṭikāmoda is vīṭikā + āmoda 'fragrance' (the long ā absorbs āmoda's initial ā).

report.summary: Checked all 26 names of ślokas 1–10 against text.json: sandhi at every member junction (and at visible prefix junctions such as ud + jvalā), a layered samāsa analysis with vigraha-vākyas written word by word in pausa form, and the meanings against that analysis. One word boundary was wrong in the old reading form and split (15: vibhrājad-alika, not vibhrāja-dalika) and one member was misidentified (26: āmoda 'fragrance', not moda); name 16's meaning missed the face-as-moon compound and was replaced. No problem was found in the Sanskrit text; no external sandhi joins names in these ślokas.
